comments.body:
Merging a DUPLICATE I filed into this one. I created c5ca-b32b-5e9e-4053 (rebellious-tyrannous-kitty) for the same defect 14 seconds after this ticket existed, because I did not search before filing. This ticket is authoritative -- it was first and it already carries file_impact and the discovered_from link. c5ca is being closed as a duplicate.

Carrying over the two acceptance criteria from mine that may not be in yours, since they are the ones that stop a concurrency fix from being self-satisfying:

DEFECT-SEEDED PROOF. Restoring the unlocked fast path must make the reproduction test fail again --
demonstrate by mutation, then revert. This matters more than usual here: a race test that passes
because the race did not happen to fire is indistinguishable from one that passes because the race is
fixed. The mutation is what tells them apart.

REPRODUCTION MUST BE DETERMINISTIC, NOT STATISTICAL. AC1 should force the interleaving -- hold the
lock while a bundle is half-created, or stub the filesystem state the fast path inspects -- rather
than running N workers and hoping. A race asserted only by repetition is not a reproduction, and the
project's standing rule is that acceptance criteria are verifiable in real time on demand.

Also worth pinning explicitly: verify with BOTH check_mechanism_delta.py --check AND
tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py. This should be a movement of an existing check rather than new
machinery, so it should register no mechanism -- and make lint alone does not cover that test, which
is the gap that sent a sibling change to Gerrit red earlier today.

Context for whoever picks this up: this is NOT a regression introduced by change 2600. Before it
there was no lock at all and workers raced freely; 2600 narrowed the window substantially and this
closes the remainder. The fix is cheap -- an flock on a local file costs microseconds and is taken a
handful of times per run, during collection and therefore off any test's timeout budget.

comments.body:
Fix pushed as Gerrit change 2613 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2613), commit cdd9e3a9439a on branch fix-toolchain-lock-fastpath from origin/main 668523feffde.

PLAN REVIEW: PASS, signed (verified_at_sha 668523feffde, material_fingerprint b4a4a637e55d5ee3), 0 blocking / 2 advisory (E6 wanted a named cardinality oracle for the cold run; P6 flagged one compound AC line). No build-drift warning was emitted -- the running build IS the worktree build at the pinned SHA, so the advisory drift probe stayed silent by design.

WHAT CHANGED
- tests/e2e/_toolchain.py: the pre-lock `if _satisfied(...): return` is gone. Readiness, the `npm` lookup, and both steps are now answered inside `with _install_lock(js_dir)`. Moving the npm lookup in with it preserves the old behaviour that an already-provisioned tree on a host without npm returns cleanly instead of newly raising.
- tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py: added the forced-interleaving reproduction; extended the two-process oracle's stub to bracket `npm run build` as well as the install, asserting every span closes before the next opens across both processes and both steps.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION (not statistical). A peer process takes the flock and, WHILE HOLDING IT, creates exactly the state the unlocked check inspects -- node_modules/, node_modules/playwright/, and a half-written dist/roundtrip.mjs -- appends peer-mid-build to an append-only log, sleeps 2s, appends peer-done, then releases. The test waits for peer-mid-build to be on disk (a precondition, not a hoped-for race), calls provision_toolchain, and appends caller-returned. The oracle is the ORDER.

RED against the unfixed code, verbatim:
  E  AssertionError: the caller returned while a peer still held the lock over a half-written bundle - a readiness check ran outside the lock: ['peer-mid-build', 'caller-returned', 'peer-done']
  E  assert ['peer-mid-bu..., 'peer-done'] == ['peer-mid-bu...ler-returned']
  E  At index 1 diff: 'caller-returned' != 'peer-done'
  1 failed, 19 deselected in 2.70s

DEFECT-SEEDED PROOF. With the fix in place, re-inserting `if _satisfied(js_dir, with_browser=with_browser): return` above the `with _install_lock(...)` block reproduced the identical failure ("At index 1 diff: 'caller-returned' != 'peer-done'", 1 failed, 19 deselected in 2.74s). Mutation reverted (grep -c MUTATION = 0) and the module returned to 20 passed.

GATES, all from the worktree venv:
- pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q: 20 passed in 12.28s
- cold single-worker pytest tests/e2e -q over an empty tests/e2e/js: 32 passed in 358.93s, and an npm shim on PATH logged EXACTLY two invocations -- "ci" then "run build". That is the cardinality oracle the E6 advisory asked for.
- make lint: exit 0 (module-size, complexity-baseline and mechanism-delta ratchets included)
- make typecheck: exit 0, 755 source files
- scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check: exit 0, new=2 increased=0 stale=0 -- both "new" are ADMITTED pre-existing ci_gate entries from the aa9e scanner lane on main, not from this change
- pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q: 31 passed
No mechanism added, no `# mechanism-ok:` marker added. This is a movement of an existing check.

Gerrit change 2613, patch set 2 (357182c8dcf0): LLM-Review +1 (PASS, no findings), Verified -1.

Patch set 1's LLM-Review +1 carried one advisory: AC4 -- an already-satisfied tree on a host WITHOUT npm returns cleanly -- had no test. That gap was real, so patch set 2 adds test_a_satisfied_tree_needs_no_npm_on_path: provision a tree with the stub npm, then empty PATH and provision again; it must not raise and must invoke npm zero further times. Mutation-checked: restoring the npm lookup+raise ABOVE the readiness check makes it fail with 'e2e toolchain: `npm` not on PATH'; reverted. Module now 21 passed. Patch set 2's LLM-Review is a clean PASS with no advisories.

The Verified -1 has ONE failing job: scanner-integration (pinned Semgrep + Gitleaks contracts), FAILED after 0m40s. That is the known repo-wide failure owned by 90c7 -- it fails on every change and on main itself -- and is not caused by this change. Every other job succeeded, including lint + type-check, the full pytest matrix (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos py3.13), optionality, artifact-probe, mutation shard selection, eval-discipline, golden-path, verify-identity and pip-audit. Notably there was NO 'worker gw0 crashed' / 'node down' on tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py, so the 9a17 signature did not recur on this base.

No recheck posted. Ticket deliberately left in_progress -- the change has not landed.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py::provision_toolchain` evaluates `_satisfied()` BEFORE taking the
`flock`, and `_satisfied` treats the harness bundle as ready on mere existence
(`(js_dir / BUNDLE_RELPATH).is_file()`). esbuild writes `dist/roundtrip.mjs` in place, so
under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` a worker can observe the path exist while the lock holder is
still writing it, return early from the unlocked fast path, and run
`node dist/roundtrip.mjs` against a truncated file. The failure surfaces as a confusing
harness/JSON error rather than as a provisioning problem.

Raised as an LLM-Review advisory on change 2600 (`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:151`). NOT a
regression from 2600: before it there was no lock at all and workers raced freely; 2600
narrowed the window and this closes the remainder. History and the duplicate-merge notes are
in the comments.

## Approach

Delete the unlocked fast path; evaluate `_satisfied()` INSIDE `_install_lock`. The `npm`
lookup moves inside the lock too, after the readiness check, so an already-provisioned tree
on a host without `npm` still returns cleanly rather than newly raising. This is a MOVEMENT
of an existing check, not new machinery: no new lock, env var, config key, feature flag, CI
gate, fixture or helper, so the mechanism-delta ratchet must stay at zero.

An `fcntl.flock` on a local file costs microseconds and is taken a handful of times per run
(once per xdist worker at collection, plus at most once per session in the fixture
fallback), so the fast path buys almost nothing while creating the window. A waiter blocks
only while a peer is genuinely provisioning, and it waits during COLLECTION, which is off
every test's timeout budget - the property bug 9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091 established.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` - move the `_satisfied()` and `npm`-lookup checks inside
  `_install_lock`; drop the pre-lock fast path.
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` - add a deterministic forced-interleaving
  reproduction, and extend the existing two-process concurrency oracle to bracket the build
  step as well as the install.

## Reproduction strategy

The reproduction FORCES the interleaving; it does not spawn N workers and hope. A child
process takes the provisioning `flock`, and while HOLDING it creates exactly the state the
fast path inspects - `node_modules/`, `node_modules/playwright/`, and a half-written
`dist/roundtrip.mjs` - appends `peer-mid-build` to an append-only log, sleeps, appends
`peer-done`, and only then releases. The test waits for `peer-mid-build` to appear (so the
half-written state provably exists first), calls `provision_toolchain`, and appends
`caller-returned`. The log order is the oracle:

- pre-fix the unlocked fast path fires immediately and the log reads
  `peer-mid-build, caller-returned, peer-done`;
- post-fix the caller blocks on the lock and it reads
  `peer-mid-build, peer-done, caller-returned`.

No sleep-and-hope, no repetition: the interleaving is constructed, so the RED is reproducible
on demand in real time.

The existing two-process test brackets only the install step; its stub is extended to bracket
`run build` as well, and it asserts every span in the merged log closes before the next one
opens, across both processes and both steps.

Uncontended behaviour is confirmed unchanged by the rest of the module, which already pins
the no-op-when-satisfied case, the missing-`npm` case, the unusable-lock case, the
without-then-with-browser completion case, and a real nested pytest collection that asserts
exactly one install per selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `provision_toolchain` performs NO readiness check outside the lock: reading
      `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` shows the `_satisfied()` call only inside the
      `with _install_lock(js_dir):` block, and no `return` precedes it.
- [x] A caller never returns while a peer is mid-build, proven DETERMINISTICALLY by the
      forced-interleaving test described above (constructed lock-held half-written state, not
      repetition).
- [x] DEFECT-SEEDED PROOF: restoring the unlocked fast path makes that test FAIL again. The
      mutation output is quoted in the ticket trail and the mutation reverted - a race test
      that passes because the race did not fire is otherwise indistinguishable from one that
      passes because the race is fixed.
- [x] An already-satisfied tree on a host with no `npm` still returns cleanly (no new
      `npm not on PATH` failure introduced by moving the lookup under the lock).
- [x] No regression in the uncontended path: the whole existing provisioning module passes,
      and a cold single-worker run provisions exactly once.
- [x] No new mechanism is registered, and no `# mechanism-ok:` marker is added.

## Testing

Each criterion names the command that proves it, run from the worktree venv
(`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" ...`):

- AC1 (no unlocked check): `git diff` on `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py`, plus
  `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q`.
- AC2 (deterministic reproduction):
  `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q -k half_written` - GREEN
  after the fix.
- AC3 (defect-seeded proof): re-insert the pre-lock
  `if _satisfied(js_dir, with_browser=with_browser): return`, re-run the AC2 command and
  observe RED with the interleaved log in the assertion message, then `git checkout` the
  mutation away and re-run to GREEN.
- AC4 (satisfied tree without npm):
  `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q -k "satisfied or missing_npm"`.
- AC5 (no regression): `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q` in full,
  and a cold `python -m pytest tests/e2e -q -p no:randomly --collect-only` over a cleaned
  `tests/e2e/js` showing one install and one build.
- AC6 (ratchets): `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` AND
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q` - BOTH, because `make lint` runs
  only the first and that gap has already sent a sibling change to Gerrit red.
- Whole-tree gates: `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

file_impact.reason: move the _satisfied() readiness check inside _install_lock so no caller can observe a half-written harness bundle through the unlocked fast path
extend the two-process concurrency oracle to bracket the build step as well as the install, and assert both spans are disjoint across processes
